item.title: Aikido: Strength, Balance and Self-defense — Tue Aug 25, 7:00 AM — Abel de Luna Community Center
item.description:
Explore the art of Aikido—a dynamic martial art that develops **confidence, fitness, balance, awareness, and practical self-defense skills**. **Registration is now open**.
This 16-class series introduces the fundamental techniques and philosophy of Aikido, along with useful skills drawn from other martial arts. You’ll learn practical ways to protect yourself while developing greater coordination, balance, flexibility, and harmony—both on and off the mat.
Classes feature **individualized instruction** in a supportive and welcoming environment. Whether you’re completely new to martial arts or have previous experience, you’ll have an opportunity to learn at your own pace.
**Sensei Chris King** has more than 30 years of experience practicing and teaching both Zen and Aikido.
**No previous martial arts experience is required.** **Come try a class—your first class is FREE!**
**Tuesdays • 5:30–6:30 pm,** **August 25 through December 15**
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Fifteen Minutes for Moms at Sebastopol Center for the Arts — Wed Aug 26, 11:00 AM — Sebastopol Center for the Arts
item.description:
This series of short, practical talks is designed to give mothers and caregivers simple, actionable tools to support their financial security, physical health, and mental well-being. Each session is 15 minutes or less and focuses on one key topic participants can immediately put into practice. Topics include: Money for Moms - Understanding Social Security benefits and simple strategies to strengthen future retirement income while raising young children. Stress Relief & Pelvic Stability Through Breathwork - A five-minute breathing routine to reduce stress and support pelvic and postural health. Fighting Anemia & Essential Postpartum Health Checks - Important information on anemia, iron and ferritin levels, Vitamin D, thyroid health, and other key postpartum screenings.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

Arrive at the studio by 10:15 AM to sign up for the list. Each poet takes turns at the mic for a max of 3 minutes each. Depending on number of poets there may be multiple rounds.
The show can be heard worldwide through the TuneIn app, internet streaming services, or in Vallejo over the airwaves at 89.5 FM.

item.description: Habrá servicio de interpretación al español Join us for this free educational seminar open to all Sonoma County employers, business leaders, HR professionals, and managers. The first session of this three-part series explores the Pregnant Worker Fairness Act and practical strategies for supporting employees during pregnancy, after childbirth, and throughout the transition to parenthood. Presented by Samantha Pungprakearti, Associate, Carle, Mackie, Power & Ross LLP, the seminar combines expert employment legal reminders with discussion of innovative workplace practices that help employers attract, retain, and support talented employees through work-life balance initiatives. Participants will learn: What accommodations employers may be required to provide during pregnancy and after childbirth—and why those obligations are broader than many employers realize. item.description:
Price: Adult $10, Senior/Full Time Student $5 \(Plus a $2 p er ticket service Charge Online\)
Ticket Info:
Sponsor: Marin Center
Link: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/cu
The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Marin County Civic Center is a national- and state-designated historic landmark. Ninety minute docent-led tours of the Civic Center are offered every Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 am, leaving from the second floor Café, Room 233. The cost is $10 adults and $5 seniors and students. No reservations are required. Groups of ten or more can arrange a private docent tour by calling the Visitor Services Office at \(415\) 473-3762.

Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Aikido: Strength, Balance and Self-defense — Sun Aug 30, 7:00 AM — Abel de Luna Community Center
item.description:
Explore the art of Aikido—a dynamic martial art that develops **confidence, fitness, balance, awareness, and practical self-defense skills**. **Registration is now open**.
This 16-class series introduces the fundamental techniques and philosophy of Aikido, along with useful skills drawn from other martial arts. You’ll learn practical ways to protect yourself while developing greater coordination, balance, flexibility, and harmony—both on and off the mat.
Classes feature **individualized instruction** in a supportive and welcoming environment. Whether you’re completely new to martial arts or have previous experience, you’ll have an opportunity to learn at your own pace.
**Sensei Chris King** has more than 30 years of experience practicing and teaching both Zen and Aikido.
**No previous martial arts experience is required.** **Come try a class—your first class is FREE!**
**Tuesdays • 5:30–6:30 pm,** **August 25 through December 15**
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Sun Aug 30, 8:00 AM — Marin County Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Free Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market. Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine. www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian
